newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH UNIONS, EMPLOYERS SAY SET NEW FRAME DEAL.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH UNIONS, EMPLOYERS SAY SET NEW FRAME DEAL.

text.p: Two key labour market lobbies, the Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK) and the Confederation of Finnish Industry and Employers, said on Friday they had set a new, clearer and more flexible frame agreement.
The new deal "reduces too detailed central union level agreements, simplifies practices and moves decision-making to union and workplace level," the lobbies said in a statement.

SAK chairman Lauri Ihalainen told a news conference that this would not as such have a direct impact on the next round of pay talks but that it showed TT wanted to preserve the labour market system, as it did in a recent joint EMU declaration.
"This has the same tone, it is important in the sense that it shows that there is a will to continue keeping (centralised) labour market talks," Ihalainen said.
However, TT said it was important that the new umbrella deal gave unions the liberty to agree differently branch-by-branch when necessary.

Another addition in the new deal -- which cuts the text to almost a quarter of the previous agreement, making it easier for employers and union representatives to comply with -- was that unions would have to announce sympathy strikes and political strikes four days in advance.
